newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian police bust Nigerian prostitution ring.
newsitem.headline: Belgian police bust Nigerian prostitution ring.

text.p: Belgian police have smashed a major prostitution ring involving Nigerian girls brought into the country on forged papers and sold into sexual slavery.
"We are still investigating, but we know that at least 300 girls passed through this ring," Gendarmerie Captain Bernard Libbrecht told RTBF television on Tuesday.

So far the police have arrested 12 people in connection with the ring which he said also involved Italy, the Netherlands and Germany, although the girls mostly ended up as prostitutes in Antwerp and Brussels.
Libbrecht said the ring paid 250,000 francs ($8,300) a girl, part in advance with the balance on delivery.
La Derniere Heure newspaper said once sold, the girls could only buy themselves out for 750,000 francs ($25,000).
It said the head of the ring, known as "the pastor", ran his business from Germany but paid frequent visits to Brussels to take orders for girls before going to Nigeria to get them.
The newspaper said "the pastor" picked only the prettiest girls and persuaded them to come to Europe where their beauty would be better appreciated.
He gave them forged passports but then took them back once they arrived in the country.
La Derniere Heure said that frequently the girls found that the only way they could survive was to take an active part in the trade.
Police found out about the trade a year ago after two of the girls volunteered information.
